faqs.q: Why is office cleaning so expensive in San Jose, CA?
faqs.a: San Jose's 1.33x multiplier reflects a $21.95/hr median janitor wage reference, city-indexed minimum wage ordinances, California AB 1978 registration and training compliance, high workers' compensation and liability costs, and LEED green-cleaning requirements—putting standard billed rates at $47 to $80 per hour.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to clean a 5,000 sq ft office in San Jose?
faqs.a: For commercial carpet and two restrooms, 5,000 sq ft cleaning in San Jose averages $2,972 to $5,010/month (1x/wk), $5,529 to $9,329/month (2x/wk), $7,910 to $13,357/month (3x/wk at 13.0 visits), and $12,526 to $21,164/month (5x/wk at 21.65 visits) before add-ons.

faqs.q: What happens if a San Jose office hires an unregistered cleaning contractor?
faqs.a: Under California AB 1978, commercial property managers and tenants who contract with an unregistered janitorial vendor risk joint and several civil liability for wage-and-hour violations and statutory penalties. Always verify active DIR registration before contract award.

faqs.q: How should annual wage increases be handled in San Jose janitorial contracts?
faqs.a: Because San Jose adjusts its municipal minimum wage annually for CPI, most multi-year contracts include an explicit statutory wage pass-through clause alongside a 3% to 5% cap on non-wage overhead escalations. Require transparent payroll documentation before approving mid-contract hikes.

faqs.q: What tasks are excluded from standard San Jose monthly office cleaning quotes?
faqs.a: Routine nightly pricing excludes clean-room gowning/ISO certification protocols, polished concrete diamond honing or carpet extraction ($0.040–$0.080/sq ft/month amortized), paper and soap consumables ($0.012–$0.025/sq ft/visit), and high exterior glazing above reach.
